I read the whole file. I did not open the imported modules, so I did not check whether they already hold a shared lemma for any of these patterns.

I looked at these repeated patterns and rejected each one:

1. The roughly 30 `_mem_FP` theorems all use `simpa only [...] using! machineCompose_mem_FP ... / machinePair_mem_FP ...`. Each proof is one or two lines of combinator application. This is routine unfolding and thin wrapping of existing closure lemmas, so it is not nontrivial repeated mathematical reasoning.

2. The `_encode` projection lemmas (Dimension, Precision, Tau, Delta, Upper, Matrix, Ellipsoid) each run `simp` over a growing list of unfolded accessors. This is mechanical unfolding. Any shared lemma would only restate `machinePairFirst`/`machinePairSecond` on `pair`, which `simp` already handles.

3. In `machineBetheEpigraphOracleResponseCode_encode`, the two nonlinear sub-branches both convert `(1/2)^p` to `(2^p)⁻¹` with `simpa [one_div, div_pow] using! hnonlinear`. That is a one-line calculation. Factoring it would only move duplicated branches inside a helper, which the rubric says is insufficient.

4. `scannedBetheBoundedEpigraphOracle_valid` and `scannedBetheBoundedEpigraphOracle_acceptsOnly` both derive "floor scan not found implies all entries are above delta". Each does this with `apply finalBetheFloorScanSemanticState_notFound_all_above; simpa using! hfloor`. This is already a call to an existing lemma plus a two-token side goal, so it is not a repeated proof block.

I found nothing that meets the rubric's bar of nontrivial repeated reasoning. The remaining uncertainty is limited to the imported modules, which I did not check.
